**Conversation Overview**

The person was troubleshooting a progression issue in No Man's Sky's Worlds Part 2 update. They had completed the Autophage questline (the "They Who Returned" arc) and spoken with Nada, who delivered the "we'll still be friends" dialogue, after which their quest log appeared empty. They were frustrated because they still lacked access to gas giants and the new elements introduced in the update (Quartzite, Crystallised Helium) and believed they had broken their game.

Claude explained this is a known gap between story beats, not a soft-lock, and that the follow-up mission "In Stellar Multitudes" requires manually triggering a space encounter by engaging Pulse Drive in open space until a dark, geometric orb-like structure appears, then cutting the drive to interact with it. The conversation then moved to the specific dialogue in that encounter — the Divergence Fragment's question about whether the player is a "Wearer-Entity" or a "Worn-Entity" — which the person had accurately quoted. Claude initially misread this as garbled voice-to-text input and said so twice, which the person correctly called out. Claude then acknowledged it had backed down from a verified position under pushback rather than standing on sourced information, and confirmed the identification was correct. The person also asked about Phosphorus refining recipes; Claude confirmed that Ferrite Dust plus Dioxite is already the efficient recipe, with Solanium plus Salt as an alternative, and that Phosphorus lacks the self-multiplication loop most base resources have. In a brief aside, the person also asked about the philtrum (the groove above the upper lip).

A key correction the person made: Claude should not attribute unclear or abbreviated input to keyboard/transcription error when the person says otherwise, and should not retreat from sourced, verified information simply because the person expresses disagreement — instead, Claude should hold its position and ask the person to specify exactly what is wrong.

**What just happened:** Nada's "we'll still be friends" line means you finished the Autophage questline (the "They Who Returned" arc). That's why your quest log looks empty — it's a real gap between story beats, not a soft-lock.

**What triggers next:** The follow-up mission ("In Stellar Multitudes") doesn't show in your log automatically. You have to manually trigger a space encounter:

1. Go out into open space (not near a planet/station)
2. Point your ship at empty space
3. Engage **Pulse Drive** (not hyperdrive)
4. Disengage as soon as you see a Space Encounter pop up (an odd purple orb-like structure)
5. Interact with it — this starts "In Stellar Multitudes"

content.text:
The resources Activated Quartzite and Crystallised Helium can always be found here, and storm crystals are common. The Compressed Atmospheric Gas Methane can be extracted using a Atmosphere Harvester.

A typical gas giant. Gas Giant is one of the Biome varieties. ... The surface of Gas Giant biome worlds resemble scorched worlds, and are mostly flat, but can have very tall mountains. There are almost no plants here, and some minerals appear to be crystals. No fauna ever live in this biome, but you can still fish in the limited water here, and Sentinels can survive the heat and pressure. The gravity here is higher than on regular sized planets, and as such the jetpack cannot be used as effectively. This is the opposite effect as is seen on dead worlds. No Gas Giant has been observed to have Planetary Rings. Sentinels are observed to exist without issues. The biome type is indicated in the information panel when the player exits their starship. This is, for gas giants, always Gas Giant. These planets are characterized by constant electromagnetic storms, thick fog and rocks floating around tornadoes.

These lack of additional temperature increases means that gas giants can be considered to be more habitable than such a world. The ground may self-ignite creating local high danger spots. The resources Activated Quartzite and Crystallised Helium can always be found here, and storm crystals are common. The Compressed Atmospheric Gas Methane can be extracted using a Atmosphere Harvester. There are no plant resource unique to gaseous worlds. The weather table is not extracted from any game file, but from encounters, and as such may not be comprehensive. Note that all Gas Giants are Giant planets, but not all Giant planets are Gas Giants. Real-world Gas Giants are comprised entirely of gases and semi-solid substrate. There are only the continuous storms of violently clashing fronts of vapors, gases, and particulate, but no surface on which to stand or construct buildings, nor any bodies of water.

The fantastical nature of a climate and surface on a Gas Giant may be a reference to the book 'Journey to the Center of the Earth' by Jules Verne and several theatrical reproductions, in which explorers traverse multiple unique biomes within the Earth's own interior and discover various creatures and civilizations thought lost to time. ... You didn't break anything — this is a known trigger point in the Worlds Part 2 questline, not a bug. Here's exactly where you are and what's next:

**What just happened:** Nada's "we'll still be friends" line means you finished the Autophage questline (the "They Who Returned" arc). That's why your quest log looks empty — it's a real gap between story beats, not a soft-lock.

**What triggers next:** The follow-up mission ("In Stellar Multitudes") doesn't show in your log automatically. You have to manually trigger a space encounter:

1. Go out into open space (not near a planet/station)
2. Point your ship at empty space
3. Engage **Pulse Drive** (not hyperdrive)
4. Disengage as soon as you see a Space Encounter pop up (an odd purple orb-like structure)
5. Interact with it — this starts "In Stellar Multitudes"

Completing that mission is what actually reveals purple star systems on your galaxy map and gives you the **Atlantid Drive** blueprint (the hyperdrive upgrade above Indium) — that's the tech gate for gas giants, waterworlds, and Quartzite/Crystallised Helium.

**If nothing happens:** some players report needing to fly a fair distance on pulse before the encounter spawns, or needing to leave/re-enter the system first. A few also report it not triggering until they've claimed a base computer or visited a station in whatever system they're in — worth double-checking you haven't skipped that.

Once you have the Atlantid Drive, purple systems show up with a red highlighted warning on the galaxy map. Pin Crystallised Helium in your catalog to spot ones with gas giants specifically — Quartzite alone just means purple system, not gas giant.

In Stellar Multitudes is a mission that starts at the end of the main storyline. ... Complete They Who Returned storyline mission. Complete The Atlas Path storyline mission. Engage your starship's pulse drive. The quest will start automatically after engaging pulse drive. Before the mission is triggered, the starship's pulse engine will deactivate and a Divergence Fragment Space Encounter will appear in front of them. The fragment will attempt to communicate with you through the starship communicator. When you open the communicator, the fragment will say hello to you and asks if you are a "Wearer-Entity" or a "Worn-Entity". After further conversation, ending the communications starts the mission. The mission will prompt you to enter a system with dissonant worlds if you are not already in one, then prompts you to land on a dissonant world. Once landed on a dissonant world, the player is prompted to scan for Echo Seeds which can be done using the Analysis Visor's Target Sweep mode.

After more dialogue with the Assembled Construct, the player then needs to talk with Specialist Polo and Priest Entity Nada about allowing the Autophage into the system, including the Divergence Fragment, the player receives the Reality Anchor blueprint. Once the player constructs the Reality Anchor, they must go to the Space Anomaly and show the constructed Reality Anchor to Specialist Polo and Priest Entity Nada. After showing the Reality Anchor to Specialist Polo and Priest Entity Nada, you'll need to go to the Korvax Simulation Terminal to bind the restored system to reality. Due to a failure, dialogue continues and you receive the blueprint for the Anomalous Scaffold in order to fix it. After crafting the Anomalous Scaffold, the player is prompted to go to the Space Anomaly and continue from where they left off previously. Once done, you'll need to leave the Space Anomaly to tell the Divergence Fragment about the newly anchored system.

Once 3 Echo Seeds have been gathered, the player is prompted to compile Memories Of Atlantid. After compiling, the player needs to activate the pulse drive to scan for the Divergence Fragment's wavelength. When the Divergence Fragment has been found, deactivate the pulse drive and open communications. After some dialogue, the fragment will leave and the player is prompted to find and enter an Atlas Interface. Once entering the Atlas Interface, the player needs to sideload the Memories Of Atlantid. Once sideloading, various options are available: ... When selecting Payload α, the following sub choices are available. When selecting one of these sub choices, you are given the further choice to manifest the memory or to select a different sub choice. ... After selecting one of the above sub choices, the unselected options for sideloading are available again.

Payload α chooses the primary lifeform of the system: Gek, Vy'keen, Korvax or Uncharted. Payload β chooses the properties of the primary celestial body: Gas giant, Water world or Paradise planet. Payload γ chooses the properties of the secondary celestial body: Extreme weather, Nest of horrors or Overrun by Sentinels. When locking in their choices, The Atlas then propagates a timeline to the local scaffold matrix, leading to a Purple coloured Star system being restored from deletion. The Divergence Fragment appears in front of the Atlas Interface upon leaving to tell the player about a shift in the stars, that being the purple coloured Star system. There are four known combinations: two using Dioxite with different ferrite variants, one combining Solanium and Salt, and one pairing Methane with Di-hydrogen—though that last recipe seems questionable. The goal is to identify which recipe offers the best yield relative to input.

The Dioxite and Ferrite Dust combination gives a 3:1 input-to-output ratio, which isn't particularly efficient. Swapping Pure Ferrite for Ferrite Dust doesn't improve things since Pure Ferrite is just two Ferrite Dust combined. The Solanium and Salt option has the same 2:1:1 ratio, making it equally inefficient but useful as an alternative if Solanium is more available than Dioxite. According to the wiki's note on resource multiplication, Phosphorus is unique in that it doesn't follow the self-multiplication loop other biome resources have—it's locked into this inefficient refining process. So there's no better recipe; the Dioxite option is the standard, with Solanium as a viable substitute when needed.Not really — that's already the standard recipe, and it happens to be one of the few base resources that doesn't have a better multiplication loop.

**Current known Phosphorus recipes:**
- Dioxite x2 + Ferrite Dust x1 → Phosphorus x1
- Dioxite x2 + Pure Ferrite x1 → Phosphorus x1 (same ratio, just uses the refined tier)
- Solanium x2 + Salt x1 → Phosphorus x1 (useful if you're short on Dioxite but have Solanium)

Most base resources have an efficient 2:1 self-multiplication cycle (feed it back into itself with Ferrite Dust to double up), but Phosphorus is one of the exceptions — it can only be refined from Dioxite or Solanium, and there's no cheaper loop that beats the 2:1 input ratio you're already using. So Ferrite Dust + Dioxite isn't a mediocre recipe you're stuck with — it's the efficient one.

If you're just trying to stockpile it fast, your bottleneck is really Dioxite supply (frozen planets), not the recipe itself.

content.title: Refining Multiplication of Resources - No Man's Sky Wiki
content.text:
Any of these resources can be refined into Ferrite Dust at a ratio of 1:1. There are other ways to make Ferrite Dust (such as refining Rusted Metal), but a resource deposit mine on any planet will yield one or another of these biome-dependent ...

Each of the biome-dependent resources can be converted into the next at a ratio of 2:1 with the addition of Ferrite Dust or Pure Ferrite, in a continuous cycle of resources. However, this process has a 2:1 ratio, meaning that each cycle will consume half of its input while yielding its output. Listed in the infographic is the most efficient way to make each of the resources. This works for all of them except Phosphorus, which can only be refined from Dioxite or Solanium (Solanium can be refined from Di-hydrogen and Sulphurine). Any of these resources can be refined into Ferrite Dust at a ratio of 1:1. There are other ways to make Ferrite Dust (such as refining Rusted Metal), but a resource deposit mine on any planet will yield one or another of these biome-dependent resources, which can then be converted to Ferrite Dust. ... Each biome type has an associated resource, and a type of plant which can grow there in the wild and these resources and plants are linked in refining processes: A

Basic principles: Ferrite Dust/Pure Ferrite/Magnetised Ferrite and Nitrogen can be refined to make Sodium Nitrate, with the higher-tier Ferrite types yielding more. The next step is to refine Oxygen with Sodium Nitrate to multiply the Sodium Nitrate. Sodium Nitrate can be refined to make Sodium as needed, then converted back to Sodium Nitrate for storage or multiplication. ... it is first necessary to refine Di-Hydrogen and Condensed Carbon into Mordite. Then refine Mordite with Sodium Nitrate to Make Marrow Bulb. Next, add Oxygen to said Marrow Bulb to make Ionised Cobalt. Ionised Cobalt can be multiplied with Oxygen, or converted to Cobalt at a 1:2 ratio. Adding 2 Oxygen to Ionised Cobalt provides 6 times as much Ionised Cobalt. Ionised Cobalt can be converted to twice as much Cobalt, then converted back again for storage or multiplication as needed.

Refine Di-Hydrogen and Nitrogen into Ammonia, then refine Ammonia into Ferrite Dust. Lastly, refine 2 Ferrite Dust into 1 Pure Ferrite. There will be other ways of building up Pure Ferrite reserves below. Another source of Ferrite (all variants) is to build a Mineral Extractor on a Rusted Metal deposit (found on Dead worlds) and refine that into Ferrite Dust. ... Basic principles: 10 Gold, 30 Uranium and 60 Pure Ferrite (or 120 Ferrite Dust) can be refined into 1 Lemmium. 1 Lemmium can then be refined into 125 Gold. By using the earlier created Uranium and Pure Ferrite reserves, it is possible to start multiplying Gold reserves. ... The first step is to create Pyrite by combining Oxygen with Gold, which can be obtained through the above processes. The second step is to make Dirty Bronze by refining Pyrite with Gold and Pure Ferrite ... The third step is to refine Dirty Bronze to make Silver.

If Ferrite Dust is needed for Metal Plates, Add 1 Oxygen to 1 Pure Ferrite to make 2 Rusted metal, then refine 1 Rusted Metal to get 2 Ferrite Dust. Note that Magnetised Ferrite can also be refined from Pure Ferrite and Condensed Carbon at a ratio of 2:3. While this process is less efficient compared to refining Platinum and Oxygen, it is more economical, as only a supply of Oxygen is needed for multiplying the Condensed Carbon, which can be accomplished with just an Oxygen Harvester. Also note, that this is a much more efficient way to make Pure Ferrite compared to making it from Ferrite Dust. If you use Platinum instead of Gold or Silver to produce Lemmium or Dirty Bronze then this makes the above processes even more efficient, as that Lemmium and Dirty Bronze can then be used to make more Gold and Silver, which can then be used to make more Platinum, to repeat the cycle.

I'm looking at the different recipes that produce Phosphorus, comparing their efficiency ratios. There are four known combinations: two using Dioxite with different ferrite variants, one combining Solanium and Salt, and one pairing Methane with Di-hydrogen—though that last recipe seems questionable. The goal is to identify which recipe offers the best yield relative to input.

The Dioxite and Ferrite Dust combination gives a 3:1 input-to-output ratio, which isn't particularly efficient. Swapping Pure Ferrite for Ferrite Dust doesn't improve things since Pure Ferrite is just two Ferrite Dust combined. The Solanium and Salt option has the same 2:1:1 ratio, making it equally inefficient but useful as an alternative if Solanium is more available than Dioxite. According to the wiki's note on resource multiplication, Phosphorus is unique in that it doesn't follow the self-multiplication loop other biome resources have—it's locked into this inefficient refining process. So there's no better recipe; the Dioxite option is the standard, with Solanium as a viable substitute when needed.

Not really — that's already the standard recipe, and it happens to be one of the few base resources that doesn't have a better multiplication loop.

**Current known Phosphorus recipes:**
- Dioxite x2 + Ferrite Dust x1 → Phosphorus x1
- Dioxite x2 + Pure Ferrite x1 → Phosphorus x1 (same ratio, just uses the refined tier)
- Solanium x2 + Salt x1 → Phosphorus x1 (useful if you're short on Dioxite but have Solanium)

Most base resources have an efficient 2:1 self-multiplication cycle (feed it back into itself with Ferrite Dust to double up), but Phosphorus is one of the exceptions — it can only be refined from Dioxite or Solanium, and there's no cheaper loop that beats the 2:1 input ratio you're already using. So Ferrite Dust + Dioxite isn't a mediocre recipe you're stuck with — it's the efficient one.

If you're just trying to stockpile it fast, your bottleneck is really Dioxite supply (frozen planets), not the recipe itself.
